text:
Anya: quick follow-up from the compaction RFC — I pushed a small PR with the experimental compact-on-idle path (https://gh/rdw/compaction-pr). wanted to surface tradeoffs before we march forward.
Mike: saw it, skimmed. what's the user-visible change?
Anya: allocator will attempt in-place compaction when a staging pool has >20% fragmentation and system idle for 200ms. adds an async worker, preemptible by hot inference.
Sanjay: 200ms seems risky for tails on p99. how do we avoid stalling requests?
Anya: compactor runs at low priority and yields on any KV cache hit path. it also acquires a soft token from evictor; if token isn't available it backs off.
Lisa: can we get a short config snippet?
Anya: sure —

```
# runtime.conf
allocator.compaction.enabled = true
allocator.compaction.idle_ms = 200
allocator.compaction.fragmentation_threshold = 0.2
allocator.compaction.preemptible = true
allocator.compaction.max_workers = 2
```

Alex: two high-level concerns: 1) compaction moves data between GPU pages -> may trigger PCIe thrash, 2) we need correctness with pinned pages for CUDA.
Anya: agreed. design notes: we only compact pages that are not pinned and not in-flight (check refcount==0). we also rate-limit PCIe DMA and cap bytes/sec.
Mike: what's the metric for success? less long-term fragmentation and fewer OOMs during sustained epochs?
Anya: primary metric is fragmentation_filled_ratio and OOM_rate per tenant. secondary: p99 latency regressions during compaction windows.
Sanjay: how are we measuring fragmentation_filled_ratio?
Anya: hotset estimator + binned residency hist. simple heuristic: reclaimed_bytes / reclaimable_bytes over a 1h window.
Lisa: rollout plan? I'd prefer feature-flagged per-cluster and an automatic kill-switch if tail latency degrades >5%.
Anya: plan in PR: default off, opt-in via console flags for canary clusters, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, then gradual ramp. include circuit breaker: if p99 increases by 5% for 30m, disable.
Alex: API boundary question — should the evictor tell allocator "freeable ranges" or allocator should probe evictor? current PR has allocator asking evictor for tokens.
Sanjay: token model seems cleaner for backpressure. evictor retains global view and grants tokens. avoids races where both try to move same pages.
Mike: token model means new RPC between allocator and evictor — latency?
Anya: token grant is local IPC on the host; no remote calls. we reuse existing admission channel. negligible.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster rdw-canary-3 has runtime image: gcr/rdw/rvv:compaction-exp (deployed 6570001130).
Lisa: good. let's add synthetic load that triggers edge-case: small-batch latency + high fragmentation. we need a job that ramps small qps and holds large tensors allocated.
Alex: also add a test where CUDA pinned allocations are aggressively used to ensure compactor skips them.
Sanjay: one more thing — what about fragments across multiple GPUs (peer mapped pages)? Compaction must preserve GPU affinity or do remote copies?
Anya: current approach: only compact within same device affinity. cross-GPU compaction is out-of-scope for now; we'll flag fragments that span devices and let the global defrag job handle it later.
Mike: ok. any instrumentation? stack traces, events?
Anya: yes: compact.start/stop, compact.yield, compact.bytes_moved, compact.pcie_bps and compact.preempt_count. logging rate-limited.
Lisa: please add a lightweight histogram for time_to_reclaim per compaction run. that will show us cost per op.
Anya: will do.
Alex: last call — I worry about long tail freeze if compactor holds a mutex competing with allocation hot path. ensure we don't take allocator-wide locks.
Anya: design uses per-arena fine-grained lock and lockless freelist handoffs where possible. compactor only locks target arena briefly to splice.
Sanjay: ack. if all good, i'll help with test harness and the eviction token integration.
Anya: thanks — pushing an update this afternoon with telemetry and the circuit breaker config. canary starts tomorrow.
Mike: :thumbsup:
Lisa: thanks team.
